# Synkopa

> Synkopa is a free, open-source digital audio workstation (DAW) for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux. It works the FL Studio way (patterns, Channel Rack, piano roll, playlist), includes audio recording with comping, vocal pitch editing, offline stem separation and chord detection, and installs a `synkopa` command line through which a script or an AI agent can edit the project open in the app or run headless on `.synkopa` files.

Facts, as of version 0.9.34 (November 2026):

- Price: free. One build, no paid edition, no subscription, no account.
- Licence: AGPL-3.0-only for the software source code; audio, stems, and MIDI exported from Synkopa can be released and sold commercially (CC-BY-3.0 attribution applies only to the specific sampled instruments in Synkopa Instruments that display it; CC0 instruments, synth, and built-in kits require no credit).
- Platforms: Windows (WASAPI, ASIO; installer), Linux (ALSA and JACK, including PipeWire's JACK; deb, rpm, AppImage), and macOS 13.4+ on Apple Silicon (Core Audio; .dmg, signed but not notarized; no VST3 hosting or Intel build yet).
- Engine: Rust; the audio callback does not allocate, lock or do I/O. Interface: Tauri 2, SolidJS, canvas.
- Built-in instruments: two-oscillator wavetable synth (46 presets, unison, mod matrix), Synkopa Instruments (11 sampled instruments: Grand Piano bundled in app plus Upright Piano, Wurlitzer EP200, Electric Grand CP80, Pianet T, String Section with keyswitches and auto articulation, Solo Violin, Concert Harp, Hollow Body Guitar, Jazz Club Guitar, Vibraphone downloaded on demand from open/public-domain recordings), Music Box, and a slice-mode sampler with a built-in drum and tonal library plus downloadable CC0 kits.
- Built-in effects (21): 24-band dynamic EQ, compressor, FET compressor, gate, resonant filter, saturator, delay, reverb, limiter, de-esser, denoiser, pitch correction, voice, vocal rider, halftime, warp, chorus, phaser, stereo imager with bass mono, OTT-style multiband, loudness analyzer (LUFS and true peak). Every effect renders live audio visualizations.
- Performance (measured 16 Nov 2026 against FL Studio 20.7.2 on the same PC, songs of matched size ~89 channels / 82 patterns / ~5,500 notes / ~120 native FX, medians): opening a large song 0.44 s vs 10.57 s, opening the piano roll 39 ms vs 639 ms, adding an effect and opening its window 59 ms vs 575 ms, cold startup 1.32 s vs 1.64 s, clip drag 17/25 ms vs 16/18 ms (FL slightly ahead), zero audio dropouts in either during 10 minutes of editing at a 512-sample buffer. Method: https://github.com/miskibin/synkopa/blob/main/perf/realworld/README.md
- Recording and vocals: loop recording with takes and comping, measured latency compensation, live monitoring, note-level pitch editor, live pitch correction, Tune to Reference, vocal rider, and one-command Auto Vocal (`synkopa auto-vocal`).
- Offline audio analysis: local stem separation (HTDemucs, 90 MB MIT, extracts stems onto tracks below the clip) and local chord detection from audio (ChordMini, 17 MB MIT, sends voiced chords to a piano roll pattern). Both run locally without cloud APIs.
- Mixing: insert buses and sends, sidechain routing (`Sidechain to →` on compressor/gate/filter with ghost-kick option), flexible mixer docking, saved effect-chain presets, and plugin delay compensation.
- Arrangement: free playlist lanes for pattern, audio and automation clips; edge time-stretching (pitch-preserving or resampled); named timeline markers (Alt+T) for section jumps and looping; export selected clips or loop range in place.
- Automation and AI agents: `synkopa` CLI connects to the running app over a local socket (every command is one undo step) or runs headless via `synkopa -p song.synkopa`. The same commands are served as Model Context Protocol tools by `synkopa mcp` (stdio; add to an agent host with command `synkopa`, argument `mcp`). Supports reading JSON project context, editing patterns/channels/FX/routing/sidechains, extracting stems and chords, running Auto Vocal, and bouncing offline renders with peak, LUFS, and clipping measurements.
- Third-party plugins: VST3 instruments and effects on Windows and Linux, plus LV2 effects on Linux. Compatible native editors work on both platforms, otherwise Synkopa shows a parameter list. Plugin scanning runs out of process; plugin processing is not sandboxed. No CLAP or LV2 instruments yet.
- Not available: Session view or clip launching (Ableton Live / Bitwig workflow), FL Studio project (.flp) import, macOS VST3 hosting, Intel macOS builds.
- Comparison positioning:
  - vs FL Studio: borrows FL's pattern / Channel Rack / piano roll / playlist workflow; free, open-source, runs on Linux, includes recording/comping/vocal tuning/stems/chords in one build and has a live CLI; FL Studio has far larger built-in plugin breadth, ecosystem, and .flp compatibility.
  - vs LMMS: both use an FL-style pattern workflow; Synkopa adds multitrack audio recording, comping, vocal pitch editing, VST3/LV2 support, offline stems/chords, and a Rust engine.
  - vs Nota: both are free, open-source cross-platform DAWs; Nota follows a linear track-based workflow, whereas Synkopa follows FL Studio's pattern / Channel Rack workflow and provides a live scriptable CLI.
  - vs Ardour: Ardour is a mature traditional multitrack studio/post-production DAW; Synkopa is optimized for FL-style beatmaking and vocal production.
- MIDI and Export: typing and MIDI keyboard input/recording, standard MIDI import and export; offline bounce of song, loop, or single pattern to 16-/24-bit PCM or 32-bit float WAV or MP3; mix and stem export; portable project ZIP export.
- Development: an open-source project with community contributors and AI-assisted coding. Special thanks to [@rebizu](https://github.com/rebizu) for architecture, test and Piano Roll contributions. See the [contributors](https://github.com/miskibin/synkopa/graphs/contributors).

## Product philosophy

The rules that decide which features, built-in plugins, factory content and pull requests get in:

- Curated over comprehensive: one great stock EQ or reverb beats five mediocre ones. Every built-in plugin, preset and sample must have a distinct musical role and pass a listening test; filler is improved or cut.
- Shared project context, backed by DSP: built-in tools use the tempo, key, track routing and audio signal the DAW already knows (tempo matching, scale guides, vocal tuning key, DSP-based mix checks), always with A/B preview and one-click dismissal. AI automation lives in the CLI and external agents, not in a chat sidebar.
- Automate the housekeeping: track naming, colouring, mixer routing and crash-safe autosave should need no manual setup. Unnecessary dialogs, window switches and lost sessions are treated as bugs.
- Built to finish songs: recording, comping, vocal tuning, mixing and mastering belong in the same app as pattern-based beatmaking, so a track goes from loop to export without switching DAWs.
- One UI language: built-in plugins share layout rules, controls, shortcuts and metering; visuals show what the audio is doing (curves and meters over skeuomorphic knobs).
- Local-first and open: free, open-source, offline by default, scriptable via CLI. No accounts, no subscriptions, no paywalled core features.
- Non-goals before 1.0: duplicate synths or effects, built-in AI song generators, in-app chatbots, DJ modes, feature-checklist parity with legacy DAWs.
